sections.label: Regulating commuter conduct on buses
sections.summary: MOT intends to regulate commuter conduct to prevent inconsiderate behaviour on public buses and bus interchanges, aligning rules across trains and buses.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: As announced at the Ministry of Transport's (MOT's) Committee of Supply debate this year, we intend to regulate the conduct of commuters to prevent inconsiderate behaviour on public buses and bus interchanges.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: Through the proposed amendments, we will align the regulatory framework against inconsiderate behaviour across trains and buses.

sections.label: Raising maximum composition sum
sections.summary: Clause 4 raises the maximum composition sum under the PTC Act from $500 to $10,000, or half the maximum fine, whichever is lower.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: Third, clause 4 also raises the maximum composition sum under the PTC Act from $500 to $10,000, or half the amount of the maximum fine that is prescribed for the offence, whichever is lower.

sections.label: Legislative basis for MPA fees
sections.summary: Clause 7 provides legislative basis for MPA to collect dumping fees and validates past collection up to commencement of new provisions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: Following the Auditor-General’s Office’s FY2024/2025 report, MPA has been advised that the fees must be prescribed in legislation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: This amendment will therefore provide legislative basis for MPA to continue collecting such fees.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Mr Murali Pillai)
sentences.text: As MPA has already incurred significant costs in maintaining the deposit sites and managing dumping activities since 1996, and has been collecting fees in connection with the dumping activities, clause 7 will also validate the past collection of such fees up to the commencement of the new provisions.

sections.label: Bus Captains' pay and cost efficiency
sections.summary: Bus Captains' starting pay rose from just over $2,000 a month in 2013 to about $4,000 today, driving apparent cost efficiency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: While this has driven apparent cost efficiency, even as Bus Captains' starting pay rightly rose from just over $2,000 a month in 2013 to about $4,000 a month today, we must ask: how far can we push this?

sections.label: Projected 2025 COE revenue
sections.summary: With Category A prices recently hitting record highs, COE revenue for the Ministry in 2025 is projected to dwarf the $4.7 billion collected in 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: With Category A prices recently hitting record highs, the COE revenue for the Ministry in 2025 is projected to dwarf the $4.7 billion collected in 2024.

sections.label: Proposed COE-PT Fund
sections.summary: A dedicated COE-PT (Public Transport) Fund is proposed for the Government to consider establishing to bridge the gap and restore fairness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: To bridge this gap and restore a sense of fairness, I propose the Government consider establishing a dedicated COE-PT (Public Transport) Fund.

sections.label: Mandatory screening legal provisions
sections.summary: Legal provisions for mandatory screening, including x-ray scans and free searches, were introduced under the Rapid Transit Systems Act and implemented in phases in 2018 and 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The legal provisions for mandatory screening, including x-ray scans and free searches, were variously introduced under the Rapid Transit Systems Act and implemented in phases in 2018 and 2021.

sections.label: Threat assessment for bus screening
sections.summary: The passage asks the Minister to clarify the specific heightened threat assessment, if any, that necessitates extending free searches and mandatory screening to bus interchanges and public buses now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Can the Minister clarify the specific heightened threat assessment, if any, that necessitates extending powers of free searches and mandatory screening to our bus interchanges and onboard public buses at this time?

sections.label: Manpower for bus screening points
sections.summary: The passage asks about the projected manpower requirement to staff new screening points at bus interchanges and whether this will draw resources from other public transport operations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: What is the projected manpower requirement to staff for these new screening points at bus interchanges and will this draw resources away from other crucial public transport operations?

sections.label: Legislation empowering transport officers
sections.summary: The passage states that empowering transportation teams, security and police officers through legislation is a fundamental step and will support enforcement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Empowering our transportation teams, security and police officers through legislation is a fundamental step and will provide the necessary support for enforcement.

sections.label: Bus driver safety and enforcement
sections.summary: The passage hopes the Ministry will prioritise bus driver safety and asks whether more enforcement officers will be deployed along bus routes or if drivers can call quick response teams.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: With enforcement powers now available, I hope that the Ministry will continue to prioritise the safety of our bus drivers as well, as this is being rolled out.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Would we also be expecting more enforcement officers being deployed along bus routes as a result, or if bus drivers will be able to call for assistance from quick response teams if required?

sections.label: Bill consolidates under Bus Services Act
sections.summary: The passage states the Bill consolidates these under the Bus Services Industry Act 2015, bringing clarity and strengthening public safety, while noting transport workers' limits.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: The Bill rightly consolidates these under the Bus Services Industry Act 2015, bringing greater clarity and strengthening our public safety. ⁠But, Mr Speaker, as we enhance security, we must also remember what our transport workers are and what they are not.

sections.label: Vape offenders caught on public transport
sections.summary: Their professionalism helped lead to around 60 offenders being caught around the public transport network using vapes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: Their professionalism helped lead to around 60 offenders being caught around the public transport network using vapes.

sections.label: Penalties for abuse of transport workers
sections.summary: The Bill's penalties of up to $10,000 in fines and/or up to five years' imprisonment send a clearer message, and protections for transport workers may need strengthening.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: But I must say, they stood their ground with calm professionalism. ⁠Preventing abuse requires a comprehensive approach, but deterrence through legislation is an important part of that strategy. ⁠Today, the Penal Code and the Protection from Harassment Act provide recourse.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Punggol)
sentences.text: But the penalties under the Bill – up to $10,000 in fines and/or imprisonment of up to five years – send an even clearer message. ⁠If the clause does not currently cover abuse directed at transport workers, it is perhaps timely to strengthen these protections.

sections.label: Purpose of Bill amendments
sections.summary: The Bill's amendments strengthen enforcement levers, provide legal basis for statutory functions, ensure clarity for stakeholders and streamline operational processes across land and sea transport.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: The amendments in the Bill serve as an important purpose to strengthen enforcement levers, provide legal basis for crucial statutory functions, ensure clarity for our stakeholders and streamline operational processes across our land and sea transport sectors.

sections.label: New regulations against abusing transport workers
sections.summary: New regulations will let LTA enforcement officers take stern action against passengers who abuse public transport workers under the amended Bus Services Industry Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: While this specific offence only covers acts involving bus assets or infrastructure that endanger safety, we intend to issue new regulations that will allow LTA enforcement officers to take stern action against passengers who abuse our public transport workers under the amended Bus Services Industry Act.

sections.label: LTA bus tender two-envelope process
sections.summary: LTA evaluates bus tenders based on a two-envelope process, where quality evaluation is conducted before looking at price submissions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: LTA evaluates bus tenders based on a two-envelope process, where quality evaluation is conducted before looking at price submissions.

sections.label: Government subsidies for public transport
sections.summary: The Government provides substantial operating subsidies of $2 billion for public transport every year, more than $1 in subsidies for every journey taken.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: The public transport sector is a key area for Government investment and we already provide substantial operating subsidies of $2 billion for public transport every year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: This equates to more than $1 in subsidies for every journey taken.

sections.label: Transport ecosystem amendments
sections.summary: The Bill's amendments are part of efforts to maintain a well-governed, forward looking and trusted transport ecosystem supporting Singapore's connectivity, competitiveness and environmental sustainability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Taken together, the amendments in this Bill are part of our broader effort to maintain a well-governed, forward looking and trusted transport ecosystem – one that continues to support Singapore’s connectivity, competitiveness and environmental sustainability.
